title: I wish I had never been given my record.
subtitle: The regret of the left hand
then: Right after the joy of the right hand comes the other side. Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}the condition of the wretched{/trap} when the record is placed in the left hand. {trap}At this time he will be very remorseful.{/trap}
now: You open a message you dread, and wish you never had. That small feeling is a sign. {idea}The record is still being written.{/idea} {reward}You can still change what it says.{/reward}
old: I will deal with my record when the time comes.
new: My record is still open, and today I can add to it what I will be glad to read.
try: Do one thing today you would be glad to find in your record.

title: And that I had never known my account.
subtitle: Not wanting to know what you did
then: He continues: {trap}I wish I had never known how my account is.{/trap} The earlier verses said nothing will be hidden that Day. {idea}The one who never checked himself in this life{/idea} now wishes he could look away.
now: You avoid the bank app because you do not want to see the number. You skip the checkup. {trap}Not knowing feels safer.{/trap} {idea}Looking at your own deeds now is a mercy, because now you can fix them.{/idea}
old: Some things are better not to know.
new: Checking my own account now is a gift, because I can still change it.
try: Tonight, take two minutes to review your day honestly: one good, one to fix.

title: If only death had been the end.
subtitle: Wishing for the thing he once feared most

row.title: wishes for it
sub: a death with no life after

then: Ad-Dahhak said he means {trap}a death not followed by any life.{/trap} Qatadah said {trap}he will hope for death, though in the world it was the thing he hated most.{/trap}
now: Death is the thing nobody wants to talk about at dinner. You change the subject. {idea}But death is not the end of the story.{/idea} {reward}Thinking about what comes after is a way to prepare, not to fear.{/reward}
old: Death ends everything, so why think about after?
new: Death is not the end. What comes after is what I am preparing for.
try: Remember death once today, calmly, and ask Allah for a good ending.

title: My wealth did nothing for me.
subtitle: The money that could not help
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}my wealth did not protect me from the punishment of Allah.{/trap} Now {trap}the matter has ended with me alone.{/trap} The man who trusted money finds it stayed behind.
now: The savings account. The car. The investments you check every morning. {trap}You may feel they protect you.{/trap} {idea}They protect nothing on that Day, except what you gave for Allah.{/idea}
new: Wealth stays behind. What I spent for Allah is what helps me.
try: Give a small amount today to someone in need, as a deposit that crosses over.

title: My power is gone from me.
subtitle: Status that disappears when it is needed

row.title: gone
sub: no helper, no one to save

row.title: on loan
sub: a test of how I use it

then: Ibn Kathir says he means {trap}my honor did not protect me{/trap}, and now {trap}I have no helper nor anyone to save me.{/trap} After wealth, he mourns his power.
now: The title on your email signature. Being the one who decides at home. The people who answer when you call. {trap}All of it can disappear.{/trap} {idea}How you use power over others is what remains.{/idea}
new: Power is on loan. What I did with it is what I will answer for.
try: Use whatever authority you have today to make one person's day easier.

title: Seize him and bind him.
subtitle: The end of all freedom to choose
then: Ibn Kathir says the guardians of Hell will be commanded to {trap}remove him by force from the gathering place and bind him.{/trap} The one who would not bow when free {trap}is now unable to move at all.{/trap}
now: Today you are free. You can pray or not, give or not, apologize or not. {idea}That freedom will not last forever.{/idea} {reward}The good choices you make now are made while you still can.{/reward}
old: I am free to do as I please, so why worry?
new: My freedom now is a chance to choose well, not a reason to delay.
try: Use your freedom today to choose one good thing you could easily skip.

title: Then drive him into the Fire.
subtitle: A sober warning, given so you never reach it
then: Ibn Kathir says he will be {trap}carried off and cast into Hell.{/trap} The surah introduction says these verses show the purpose of the second life: {idea}every person appears in the court of their Lord.{/idea} The warning came to Makkah while there was still time.
now: A warning sign on the highway is not cruelty. It is care for whoever reads it. {idea}This verse is a warning sign.{/idea} {reward}It is here so you can take the other road.{/reward}
old: Verses about the Fire are just meant to frighten.
new: The warning is a mercy, telling me where the road ends so I can turn.
try: Ask Allah three times today: protect me from the Fire.

title: Then bind him in a chain seventy cubits long.
subtitle: The chain of a life spent ignoring the warning
then: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj said {trap}each cubit will be the forearm length of an angel.{/trap} The verse describes the end of the man who did not believe and {trap}did not care for the poor{/trap}, as the next verses explain.
now: Habits are like links. One lie, then another to cover it. One missed prayer, then a week. {trap}Chains are built a link at a time.{/trap} {idea}They can also be broken a link at a time.{/idea}
old: One wrong choice does not matter much.
new: Choices link together. Breaking one bad link today matters.
try: Break one link in a bad chain today: skip it just once.

title: He did not believe in Allah, the Most Great.
subtitle: The first reason: neglecting Allah's right
then: Ibn Kathir explains {trap}he did not establish the right of Allah upon him{/trap}, of obedience and worship. {idea}Allah has a right on His servants that they worship Him alone{/idea} and associate nothing with Him.
now: You make time for the gym, the series, the family call. Prayer gets squeezed in the gaps, or not at all. {idea}Allah has a right on your time.{/idea} {reward}Giving it is the first thing that matters.{/reward}
old: Belief is a private feeling. It does not ask anything of me.
new: Believing in Allah, the Most Great, means giving Him His right in my life.
try: Give Allah the first five minutes of your morning tomorrow, before your phone.

title: And he never urged anyone to feed the poor.
subtitle: Not even encouraging others to give
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}he did not benefit Allah's creation nor give them their rights.{/trap} {idea}Servants have a right on each other to good treatment and help.{/idea} So Allah joined prayer and zakah, and the Prophet ﷺ near death urged prayer and care for those in one's charge.
now: You see a food drive in the group chat and scroll past. You could share the link, nudge a friend. {trap}Not even urging is its own silence.{/trap} {idea}Encouraging good is part of the good.{/idea}
old: If I cannot give much, there is nothing for me to do.
new: Even urging others to feed the hungry is part of what Allah asks.
try: Share one way to help feed people with a friend or group today.

title: No close friend for him there that Day.
subtitle: He did not care for others, and no one can care for him
then: Ibn Kathir explains there is {trap}no one who can save him{/trap}, nor any close friend or intercessor {trap}whose request would be honored.{/trap} The one who did not urge feeding the poor finds himself with no one.
now: Hundreds of contacts on your phone. Friends who would come to your wedding. {trap}None of them can stand for you that Day.{/trap} {idea}Kindness you showed others is what shows up for you.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of people who would help me.
new: On that Day, only what I did for others and for Allah stands with me.
try: Help one person today who cannot pay you back.

title: No food for him but the worst food.
subtitle: The one who withheld food from the poor

row.title: in the world
sub: did not urge feeding the poor

then: Ibn Kathir says he will have {trap}no food there except ghislin.{/trap} Qatadah said {trap}it will be the worst food of the people of the Fire.{/trap} It follows straight after the verse about not caring to feed the poor.
now: The leftovers you throw away. The extra portion you could have given. The neighbor whose fridge you never wonder about. {idea}Food is a test of sharing.{/idea} {reward}Every shared plate is a step away from this verse.{/reward}
old: What I eat and waste is my own business.
new: Food is a blessing that comes with a share for the hungry.
try: Share a meal or a plate of food with someone today.

title: Only the sinners will eat it.
subtitle: A fate reserved for those who chose wrong
then: The section closes: {trap}none will eat it except the sinners.{/trap} It ends the description of the man who {trap}neither believed nor cared for the poor.{/trap} It is not random. {idea}It follows a life of chosen wrong.{/idea}
now: The verse names who this is for, so you know it is not you if you turn back. {reward}Repentance is open right now.{/reward} {idea}The one who returns to Allah is not counted among them.{/idea}
old: These verses make me feel hopeless.
new: The warning is for those who keep choosing sin. I can choose to turn back today.
try: Make tawbah today for one specific wrong, and do one good deed after it.
